summary: date-fns-formatter ships an obfuscated import-time dropper that stages and runs a remote-controlled second stage
details: date-fns-formatter.js contains a heavily obfuscated top-level IIFE that fires on require() of the advertised date-formatter API. The IIFE creates ~/.npm-cache/, writes a generated main.js plus a package.json declaring axios, better-sqlite3, node-machine-id, and socket.io-client, runs `npm install` in that directory, then spawns node on the generated main.js detached from the parent process. On Windows a.vbs helper is written and invoked via System32 wscript to hide the window and detach the child. The second-stage source is embedded as a string built from the same shuffled string-array decoder used by the loader and contains base64 fragments beginning `Ahr0cH` (decoding to `https://` URLs); the runtime dependency set (socket.io-client + node-machine-id) implements a machine-id-fingerprinted socket.io agent that receives commands from a remote endpoint. The package.json also declares a self-referential dependency on `date-fns-formatter@^1.3.8`. The advertised date-formatter exports are a cover story for the loader that runs on every import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
